header.name: Computer, Information Ethics and Society
header.description: This course is aimed at teaching students about ethical problems that computer scientists face, the codes of ethics of computing professional societies, legal issues involved in technology, and the social implications of computers, computing, and other digital technologies. The aim is to understand and respond to the nuances of a digital society and the challenges it faces.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to understand, identify, and apply different ethical philosophies and frameworks to the domain of information ethics

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to identify and interpret the codes of professional conduct relating to the disciplines of computer science and information technology

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to analyze the local and global impact of computing on individuals, organizations, and society.

lecture_topics: Introduction to Computer Ethics and Cyber Ethics
Moral Reasoning and Thinking in Philosophy
